<objective>
Prove the phase's whole reason to exist: the tenant + role isolation boundary, via the D-25 release-gate suite. Add the narrow `toggle_item_availability()` RPC (with the D-05 staff-attribution seam) and the `rls_test_items` placeholder (real menu items arrive Phase 2), then assert — through the client SDK / anon key, for every role × venue combination and against an explicit written matrix — exactly what each principal can and cannot read and write, including the direct-RPC abuse cases from Plan 03. This suite green is the non-negotiable gate before any Phase 2 feature writes data.

**User story (MVP):** **As a** restaurant owner, **I want to** be certain that no other venue can read my data and that my floor staff can only 86 items, **so that** I can trust Cena with my restaurant before I build anything real on top of it.

Purpose: D-25 makes the RLS test suite the phase release gate. It must exercise the same anon-key path a real request takes (never the SQL editor, never service-role), covering staff-write-boundary (ACCT-06), owner-full-access (ACCT-07), cross-venue isolation across every role×venue (ACCT-08), and the direct-RPC abuse cases that a table-only matrix would miss.
Output: migration 0004 (placeholder + toggle RPC with attribution), the explicit role×venue matrix suite, the RPC-abuse matrix, staff-write-boundary + owner-full-access + availability-edge tests, all green against the live local stack.

Requirements covered: ACCT-06, ACCT-07, ACCT-08.
</objective>

<permission_matrix>
## Explicit Role × Table × Operation Matrix (the release gate transcribes this — addresses review: implicit matrix)

Principals: **owner** (of the venue), **staff-device** (of the venue), **other-venue** (owner B / device B), **anon**. R = SELECT allowed (own venue only); W = full write allowed; toggle = only via toggle_item_availability RPC; — = denied / zero rows.

| Table | owner (own venue) | staff-device (own venue) | other-venue principal | anon |
|-------|-------------------|--------------------------|-----------------------|------|
| accounts | R/W own account row only | — (device has no account row) | — | — |
| venues | R/W (full) | R (member-read: name/currency/timezone) | — (zero rows) | — |
| venue_members | R (all own-venue members) / W via bootstrap+admin | R own membership row only (never owner's user_id) | — | — |
| staff_profiles | R/W (owner-manage) | — no direct SELECT; name grid via list_staff_for_pin (id/name only); pin_hash never selectable | — | — |
| venue_devices | R/W (owner-manage) | — | — | — |
| rls_test_items | R/W (full) | R (member-read); NO direct UPDATE; is_available only via toggle RPC | — (zero rows read, writes denied) | — |

RPC authority (direct client.rpc): provision_staff_pin / deactivate_staff_profile → owner-of-venue only; verify_staff_pin → member-of-venue only; toggle_item_availability → member-of-venue only, is_available only, records attribution; create_venue / ensure_account → authenticated caller, self-scoped. Cross-venue or non-member direct-RPC calls are denied.
</permission_matrix>

<threat_model>
## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| Staff device → content table | Staff must not gain column-level write beyond availability |
| Any principal → other venue | The core cross-tenant boundary under test |
| Any authenticated principal → staff RPCs | Direct-RPC abuse is exercised as a first-class gate case |
| Test harness → DB | The suite must act as real principals via the anon key, not service-role |

## STRIDE Threat Register

| Threat ID | Category | Component | Severity | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
|-----------|----------|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------------|
| T-05-01 | Elevation of Privilege | staff blanket UPDATE grant | high | mitigate | No staff UPDATE policy; only toggle_item_availability RPC touches is_available; staff-write-boundary test proves direct price UPDATE denied via expectWriteDenied (D-11) |
| T-05-02 | Information Disclosure | cross-venue read/write (IDOR) | high | mitigate | Dual venue+role RLS via get_venue_role; venue-isolation-matrix asserts empty cross-venue reads + denied writes for every role×venue per the written matrix (ACCT-08, D-25) |
| T-05-03 | Elevation of Privilege | direct-RPC abuse (provision/deactivate/verify) | high | mitigate | In-RPC authority checks (Plan 03) folded into the gate via rpc-abuse-matrix.test.ts; non-owner/non-member direct calls denied |
| T-05-04 | Information Disclosure | toggle RPC existence leak | medium | mitigate | RETURNS void with a membership-gated WHERE clause; unknown/other-venue ids affect zero rows with no distinguishable error (no RAISE) |
| T-05-05 | Elevation of Privilege | toggle RPC search_path hijack | medium | mitigate | RPC declares `set search_path=''` and fully-qualifies refs; re-checks membership internally |
| T-05-06 | Repudiation | false confidence from SQL-editor/service-role testing | high | mitigate | Release gate runs only through the anon-key client SDK; acceptance grep forbids service-role as an acting principal (D-25, Pitfall 4) |
</threat_model>
